historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, Vol. 13, Chapter: The Battle of Hunayn and the Conquest of Mecca. Ibn Kathir (1301-1373 AD)
historical_references.context: The term Mutakaffil (Arabic: متكفل) was used for the Muslims who had pledged to protect the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the Islamic state with their lives and wealth. This pledge was made in the aftermath of the Battle of Hunayn when the Prophet (pbuh) was returning to Medina with the spoils of war. The Prophet (pbuh) asked the Muslims to pledge allegiance to him, and those who took this pledge were known as Mutakaffilun.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah, Book 3, Chapter 18: The Prophet's Farewell Pilgrimage. Ibn Hisham (854-886 AD)
historical_references.context: During the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) Farewell Pilgrimage, he asked his companions to pledge their allegiance to Ali (ra) as his successor. Those who pledged allegiance to Ali (ra) were called Mutakallimun, and those who did not were called Mutakaffilun. The Mutakaffilun believed that the Prophet (pbuh) would appoint a caliph from among the Ansar or the Muhajirun, and they did not want to commit themselves to supporting Ali (ra) as the next caliph.
